raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
Fixes #59109

## Purpose

When running pipeline parallelism (PP > 1) in Docker with default bridge networking, PyTorch's Gloo backend resolves the container hostname to the Docker bridge IP (e.g. 172.17.0.2) instead of loopback (`lo`). This causes per-step control metadata transfers (`isend_object`) to traverse the virtual bridge network stack, adding ~535ms latency per send. As context length grows and block table metadata expands, this manifests as severe long-context decode throughput collapse (>50% regression).

This PR addresses this by:
1. Documenting the root cause, symptom, and `GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME=lo` fix in:
   - `docs/serving/parallelism_scaling.md`
   - `docs/serving/distributed_troubleshooting.md`
   - `docs/usage/troubleshooting.md`
2. Updating `init_distributed_environment` in `vllm/distributed/parallel_state.py` to:
   - Automatically default `GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME="lo"` when unset for single-node multiprocessing (`nnodes == 1` and `distributed_executor_backend in ("mp", None)`).
   - Log an informative warning if single-node PP is enabled with other executors without `GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME`.
3. Adding unit tests in `tests/distributed/test_file_store.py` verifying the defaulting, preservation, and multi-node handling.

## Why this is not a duplicate

- `gh pr list --search "59109 in:body"` returned 0 matching PRs.
- The issue has been open since 2026-09-29 with no associated pull requests.

## Test Plan & Evidence

1. Unit tests:
   ```bash
   pytest tests/distributed/test_file_store.py -k test_gloo -v
   ```
   Result: `3 passed in 0.57s`.
2. Pre-commit hooks (`markdownlint-cli2`, `ruff-check`, `ruff-format`, `typos`, `Check SPDX headers`): all passed.

AI assistance was used to analyze the codebase, draft documentation/code, and format this PR description.

+## High latency or decode collapse in Docker with Pipeline Parallelism (PP)
+
+When running pipeline-parallel inference (`pipeline_parallel_size > 1`) inside a Docker container, you may observe severe decode throughput degradation on long contexts while GPU utilization remains low (e.g. 10–20%).
+
+- **Symptom:** Profiling reveals high latency on `user_annotation gloo:send` (up to ~500ms per send during decode steps).
+- **Cause:** PyTorch's `gloo` CPU control plane resolves the container hostname to the Docker bridge IP (e.g. `172.17.0.2`) instead of the loopback interface (`lo`). Control messages (which grow with context length due to KV block table metadata) traverse the Docker bridge network stack instead of communicating over loopback.
+- **Solution:** Set `GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME=lo` inside the container or pass `-e GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME=lo` to `docker run`. For multi-node deployments across separate hosts, ensure `GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME` is set to the physical network interface (e.g., `eth0`) rather than `lo`.

@@ -56,6 +56,25 @@ vllm serve gpt2 \
      --pipeline-parallel-size 2
 ```
 
+!!! warning "Performance tip: Pipeline Parallelism in Docker / Single-Node Containers (`GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME=lo`)"
+    When running pipeline parallelism (PP) within a single container (such as Docker) or a single node where all ranks share the same network namespace, PyTorch's `gloo` backend is used for the CPU control plane (e.g. `isend_object` for per-step pipeline scheduling metadata and speculative-decode coordination).
+
+    By default, Gloo resolves the container hostname to the Docker bridge IP (e.g. `172.17.0.2`) rather than loopback (`lo`). This causes control messages to traverse the virtual ethernet bridge network stack, introducing up to hundreds of milliseconds of latency per send (~500ms). As context length increases (carrying larger block tables and metadata), this manifests as severe decode throughput collapse while GPU compute sits idle.
+
+    While vLLM defaults `GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME=lo` automatically for single-node multiprocessing deployments, if you launch containers or use custom launcher environments, ensure `GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME=lo` is set when launching Docker:
+
+    ```bash
+    docker run -e GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME=lo ...
+    ```
+
+    Or exported in the container environment before starting vLLM:
+
+    ```bash
+    export GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME=lo
+    ```
+
+    *Note:* For multi-node deployments across separate hosts, `GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME` must point to your actual network interface (e.g., `eth0`), never `lo`.
+
 ## Multi-node deployment
 
 If a single node lacks sufficient GPUs to hold the model, deploy vLLM across multiple nodes. Ensure that every node provides an identical execution environment, including the model path and Python packages. Using container images is recommended because they provide a convenient way to keep environments consistent and to hide host heterogeneity.

+## High latency or decode collapse with Pipeline Parallelism (PP) in Docker
+
+When running pipeline-parallel models (`--pipeline-parallel-size > 1`) within a single Docker container, you may experience severe throughput collapse during decode—especially as context length increases—even though GPU utilization is low (silicon idle) and CPU utilization is near zero.
+
+### Root cause
+
+vLLM uses a CPU-side `cpu:gloo` process group for pipeline-parallel coordination, sending per-step scheduler metadata and block tables between stages via non-blocking `isend_object`. In a Docker container using bridge networking, PyTorch's Gloo backend resolves the container hostname to its bridge IP (such as `172.17.0.2`) rather than `127.0.0.1` (`lo`).
+
+Consequently, every control send traverses the Docker virtual bridge network stack, incurring ~500ms of latency per send. Because payload sizes increase with context length (due to block table indices), this overhead presents as a context-dependent decode collapse that mimics a compute or memory bottleneck.
+
+### Fix
+
+Set the `GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME` environment variable to `lo` so that Gloo binds to the loopback interface:
+
+```bash
+docker run -e GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME=lo ...
+```
+
+Or within the container:
+
+```bash
+export GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME=lo
+```
+
+!!! note
+    Do not set `GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME=lo` on multi-node deployments across different physical hosts, as loopback is node-local. For multi-node setups, set `GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME` to the appropriate physical network interface (e.g., `eth0`).
+
 ## Known Issues
 
 - In `v0.5.2`, `v0.5.3`, and `v0.5.3.post1`, there is a bug caused by [zmq](https://github.com/zeromq/pyzmq/issues/2000) , which can occasionally cause vLLM to hang depending on the machine configuration. The solution is to upgrade to the latest version of `vllm` to include the [fix](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/6759).
